ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, isosceles right triangles are constructed externally on each side of $\triangle ABC$ using the sides of $\triangle ABC$ as the right angles. If $AB = \sqrt{3}$, what is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $ABC$ is a right-angled triangle,\\
we have $AC^{2}+BC^{2}=AB^{2}=3$,\\
thus, the area of the shaded region $S_{\text{shaded}}= \frac{1}{2} AC^{2}+ \frac{1}{2} BC^{2}+ \frac{1}{2} AB^{2}= \frac{1}{2} (AC^{2}+BC^{2})+ \frac{1}{2} AB^{2}= \frac{1}{2} AB^{2}+ \frac{1}{2} AB^{2}=AB^{2}=\boxed{3}.$

method.method_draft: View each shaded isosceles right triangle as exactly one half of a square constructed on the corresponding side of triangle ABC. From the image, ABC is a right triangle with right angle at C, and the shaded triangles correspond to sides AC, BC, and AB. By the Pythagorean square-area theorem, the square on hypotenuse AB has area equal to the sum of the square areas on AC and BC. Hence the two shaded half-squares on AC and BC together have area equal to one half of the square on AB. The shaded triangle on AB is the other half of a square on AB. Therefore the total shaded area equals one full square on AB, namely AB^2 = (sqrt(3))^2 = 3.
